q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT DISTINCT s1.beer, s1.price, s1.bar FROM serves AS s1 JOIN serves AS s2 ON s1.bar = s2.bar GROUP BY s1.bar, s1.price, s1.beer HAVING s1.price = MIN(s2.price)

Q2, on the other hand, uses a JOIN with itself to find the minimum price for each beer at each bar and then selects the distinct beer, price, and bar. The difference arises because Q1 does not ensure that the minimum price is unique for each beer at each bar, while Q2 does.
